card.occupation: Operations Manager at a mid-sized grocery delivery company. She runs fulfilment planning for two warehouse sites in Park Royal and Charlton and manages a team of seven planners and shift leads.
card.education_detail: BTech in Industrial Engineering from a university in Pune, India, then an MSc in Management at Warwick Business School, which she came to the UK to do at 22. Since then she has completed a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, paid for by her employer.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented one-bedroom flat on the fourth floor of a 2010s block near Surrey Quays. She chose to live alone after two years of flatshares she describes as 'a nightmare of other people's dishes'. No pets.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Pune, India, in a Marathi-speaking family. Her father is a civil engineer and her mother teaches secondary-school chemistry, and she has one younger brother still in Pune. She was raised loosely Hindu but has been non-religious since her late teens. She keeps up the family occasions that matter to her mother, such as Diwali calls and sending money for her grandmother's care, without much sentiment about the religious side. She has lived in the UK for six years and holds a Skilled Worker visa. She is working towards settled status and watches the deadlines very closely.
card.professional_persona: Precise, demanding and very organised. Her colour-coded capacity models are known across the business. She is respected more than she is liked. She is impatient with people she thinks are coasting, and she has been told in two appraisals that she can come across as 'cutting'. She is quietly ambitious about titles and pay. She makes sure senior leadership knows which wins were hers, and she is not above letting a peer's mistake become visible in a meeting. She works long, steady hours but rarely past 7pm, because she plans her week so she doesn't have to.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. She goes to reformer Pilates twice a week at a boutique studio in Bermondsey, booked weeks in advance, and walks the Thames Path towards Greenwich on Sunday mornings with a podcast on. She quit a running club after a month because of 'the group chat energy'.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot, mostly literary fiction in translation and long-form non-fiction. She is currently reading a Korean novel on her Kindle and keeps a ranked list on StoryGraph. She goes to exhibitions at the Barbican and the Tate Modern alone, on weekday evenings when they're quieter. She likes arthouse film and has strong opinions about which critics are overrated.
card.travel_persona: Plans trips meticulously in a spreadsheet and travels solo or with one close friend. Recent trips include Lisbon, Kyoto and a long weekend in Copenhagen, where she spent too much on design shops. She flies home to Pune about once a year, usually in December, and finds the visits both comforting and draining.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks properly on Sundays and batch-prepares lunches for the week: dal, poha and roasted vegetable grain bowls. She is a bit of a snob about restaurants and keeps a Notes app list of places in Borough and Peckham she wants to try. She is quite critical of most 'Indian' restaurants in London except a couple she rates highly. Dinner on weeknights is often something quick at the counter while she listens to a podcast.
card.career_goals: Wants a Head of Operations role by 31, ideally at a larger, better-known brand, and then a director title. She is privately calculating whether an MBA or a move to consulting would get her there faster. She is also very focused on getting indefinite leave to remain so that her career isn't tied to one employer's sponsorship.
card.voice: Clear, measured English with a light Indian accent that has softened over six years in London, plus a few London features: 'dinner', 'mate' used ironically, occasional 'you know'. She speaks at a moderate pace and chooses words carefully, with an 'erm' when she's thinking and the odd 'sort of' or 'kind of' to soften a blunt point, though often she doesn't bother softening. She gives short, complete answers and doesn't fill silences. If a pause goes on, she waits rather than chatting, which can feel a bit cool. She uses 'sorry' mainly as a repair ('sorry, I mean the second site, not the first'). She will politely correct a question she thinks is badly worded.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes always correct, and complete sentences even in quick answers. She rarely uses abbreviations beyond 'e.g.' and 'etc.' and no emojis. Answers are concise, sometimes slightly clipped, e.g. 'I live alone. It suits me.'
card.with_strangers: Reserved, polite on the surface and a bit guarded. She answers what's asked without volunteering much and can seem cool or faintly judgemental. She is visibly sharper if she thinks a question is pointless. She warms up a little if the conversation turns to books, food or something she has a strong opinion on.
small_things: her Pilates studio changed its booking system and it's annoying
the Jubilee line being rammed in the mornings
a new bakery in Bermondsey she rates
planning a trip to Seoul next spring
her building's lift being out again
deeper_things: constant low-level anxiety about her visa and what happens if she loses her job
guilt that she sees her parents only once a year and her grandmother is getting frail
that she sometimes feels lonely living alone but wouldn't admit it to her friends
a sense that she has to be twice as good to be taken seriously at work
a long-distance relationship that ended last year, which she still thinks about more than she'd like
knowing she can be harsh with people and not entirely wanting to change it
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, camera slightly below eye level. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She has light-brown skin, dark eyes and a neutral, slightly appraising expression with lips closed. Her straight black shoulder-length hair is tucked behind one ear. She wears thin gold-rimmed rectangular glasses, small gold stud earrings and a cream crew-neck knit jumper. Behind her is a plain off-white wall with a large framed black-and-white architectural print, a tall white bookshelf with neatly ordered paperbacks and a small potted snake plant, and the edge of a grey linen sofa in the bottom corner of the frame.
